primitives.name: Sinkhorn-Knopp Optimal Transport
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'Π': 'Transport plan matrix (dimensionless)', 'U(r,c)': 'Set of transport plans with marginals r and c (dimensionless)', 'C': 'Cost matrix (units of energy or distance)', 'ε': 'Regularization parameter (dimensionless)', 'H(Π)': 'Entropy of transport plan (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: The cost matrix C is known; transport plans must satisfy marginal constraints; regularization ensures convergence.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When ε → 0, the solution approaches the exact optimal transport; when ε → ∞, the solution becomes uniform.

layer2.mapping: Maps team offensive/defensive EPA distributions to aligned strategic states via entropic regularization.
layer2.telemetry: Effective number of teams in league (N_eff) and normalized team performance metrics.

primitives.name: Empirical Bayes Shrinkage
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\hat{\\theta}_{\\text{EB}}': 'Shrunken estimate of team EPA (EPA per play)', '\\bar{y}_{\\text{W1..W7}}': 'Sample mean EPA over weeks 1–7 (EPA/p)', '\\mu_0': 'Prior mean EPA (EPA/p)', '\\tau^2': 'Variance of true team effects (EPA²/p²)', '\\sigma^2': 'Within-team variance (EPA²/p²)', 'n': 'Number of observations (plays)'}
primitives.assumptions: Normality of sample means; known within-team variance; prior distribution is normal.
primitives.breakdown_regime: As n increases, shrinkage diminishes; as τ² grows relative to σ², more shrinkage occurs.

layer2.mapping: Provides stable estimates of team EPA by combining sample data with prior expectations.
layer2.telemetry: Effective sample size (N_eff) and posterior variance of EPA estimates.

primitives.name: Davies Injury Load Multiplier
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'N_{\\text{eff}}': 'Effective number of independent samples (dimensionless)', 's_i': "Standard deviation of player i's contribution (EPA/p)", 'M_{\\text{load}}': 'Injury load multiplier (dimensionless)', 'N_{\\text{eff,league}}': 'League-wide effective sample size (dimensionless)', 'N_{\\text{eff,team}}': 'Team-specific effective sample size (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Player contributions are normally distributed; independence across players; bounded clipping range.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If team N_eff is much smaller than league N_eff, M_load > 1 indicating higher risk.

layer2.mapping: Adjusts team performance metrics based on injury risk and sample stability.
layer2.telemetry: Clipped injury load multiplier and effective sample sizes per team.

The Sinkhorn-Knopp algorithm provides a computationally efficient method for solving optimal transport problems by introducing entropy regularization. It maps discrete probability distributions (e.g., team offensive/defensive EPA) onto one another through a cost matrix, enabling alignment of strategic states. This is particularly useful in modeling how teams adapt their strategies based on opponent behavior. The empirical Bayes shrinkage estimator reduces noise in small-sample EPA estimates by borrowing strength from a global prior, improving forecast accuracy. The Davies injury load multiplier adjusts these estimates according to team-specific variability and injury risk, ensuring robustness against sampling fluctuations. Together, they form a coherent mathematical pipeline that supports both predictive modeling and tactical decision-making in GSI and GSE.
